title: Add Two Numbers
statement: Two non-empty linked lists each hold the digits of a non-negative number, with the ones digit first. Add the two numbers and return the sum in the same format: a linked list of digits, ones digit first.

example.caption: 342 + 465 = 807. The lists are written backwards, so 807 is stored as 7, 0, 8.

idea.sentence: The ones digit comes first, so walk both lists together and add column by column like on paper, passing the carry along.

jargon.plain: The tens part of a column sum (0 or 1 here). It is added into the next column.
A throwaway first node for the answer. It saves a special case for creating the first digit.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the digit lists, ones digit first, e.g. [2,4,3], [5,6,4]

compare.bruteLabel: Convert both lists to numbers, add, convert back

rows.name: Convert, add, convert back
rows.note: Looks simple, but long lists overflow a normal integer. It breaks on 100-digit inputs.

rows.name: Column by column
rows.note: Never builds a big number. The answer list is the output, so it is not extra space.

fast.takeaway: The digit-by-digit version is the same speed and never overflows, because a column sum is at most 19.

stages.title: Fake head, tail, carry
stages.note: Set up the answer list with a dummy node, a tail pointer and carry = 0.

stages.title: Add one column
stages.note: Add the current digit of l1 (or 0), the current digit of l2 (or 0) and the carry.

stages.title: Keep digit, set carry
stages.note: sum mod 10 becomes a new node. sum div 10 is the new carry.

stages.title: Next column
stages.note: Move l1 and l2 forward if they still have nodes.

stages.title: Return dummy.next
stages.note: Skip the fake node. The answer is already in ones-first order.

edges.title: Zero plus zero
edges.why: One column gives 0. The answer must still have one node, not an empty list.

edges.title: Carry out of the last column
edges.why: Both lists end but carry is 1. The loop keeps going to write that last digit.

edges.title: Different lengths
edges.why: A missing digit counts as 0. The carry still ripples through the longer list.

edges.title: A long chain of nines
edges.why: Every column carries. 7 digits sum to 8 digits, and no integer type is involved.

gotchas.text: Keep looping while carry is non-zero, not only while a list has nodes. Otherwise 5 + 5 returns [0] instead of [0, 1].
Do not turn the lists into numbers. A 30-digit list does not fit in a 64-bit integer, and even a double loses precision after 15 digits.
sum / 10 is a float division (15 / 10 is 1.5). Use Math.floor(sum / 10). Also l1?.val ?? 0 reads a missing node as 0 without crashing.
sum / 10 on ints already truncates, so no floor is needed. But Go has no optional chaining: test l1 != nil before every l1.Val and l1.Next.
Create fresh nodes for the answer. Reusing nodes of l1 or l2 works but changes the inputs, which is surprising for callers.

recap.key: Loop while l1, l2 or carry exists. sum = digits + carry. New node sum % 10. carry = sum / 10.
recap.complexity: Time O(max(n, m)). Space O(1) besides the answer.
moves: Advance l1 and l2. Return dummy.next
